A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same frequency-domain motion-generation research despite the changed title and substantial revision. Text, equations, tables, figures, and v2's Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original Open-Sora/MVDIT experiments, loss ablations, qualitative comparisons, and a 106-participant user study.

after.justification: V2 reports original backbone comparisons, Hunyuan fine-tuning experiments, motion-complexity results, ablations, and user-study outcomes.

M1.justification: V2 removes the zero-initialized enhancement module and replaces DCT processing with FFT-based losses. Translation changes from planar/quadratic fitting to ridge-regularized planar fitting; rotation replaces temporal-peak scoring with fitted tilted-line energy; scaling replaces the arctangent trend score with absolute correlation. These substantially revise the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate OpenVID-1M text-to-video generation covering translation, rotation, scaling, and mixed natural motion. Hunyuan adds a model, while the simple/complex analysis partitions existing test prompts; neither establishes new dataset, domain, or task coverage.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained Open-Sora and MVDIT baseline comparisons, v2 Table 2 adds Hunyuan comparisons against the original backbone, base-loss LoRA fine-tuning, and RAFT-based flow-consistency LoRA fine-tuning. The flow-loss comparator substantially strengthens the comparison set beyond vanilla generators.

E3.justification: V2 introduces Hunyuan experiments with frozen backbone weights and matched LoRA placement, rank, and training schedule across objectives. It also introduces GPT-5-assisted simple/complex prompt stratification. The stated four-epoch training budget, EvalCrafter metric suite, and 106-participant, 15-trial user-study design are retained.

E4.justification: V2 removes the enhancement-plus-loss versus loss-only analysis, retains the individual-loss ablation, and adds motion-complexity stratification in Table 3. Figures 2 and 4 replace and extend the qualitative cases with Hunyuan examples, including compound motions. Appendix B.10 recommends synthetic and sensitivity tests but does not report their execution.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. User-study participant counts and randomization remain unchanged. V2's theoretical noise bounds do not constitute empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds Hunyuan and motion-stratified results, removes enhancement-module result columns, and revises existing scores. For example, full-loss temporal consistency changes from 62.21 to 63.82 and Flow Score from 1.16 to 1.18 between v1 Table 3 and v2 Table 4. These accompany method changes, not controlled cross-version performance gains. User-study percentages are unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 adds a unified SIM(2) spectral formulation, identifiability and noise assumptions, residual consistency propositions, and surrogate, windowing, interpolation, and ridge bounds in Appendices A–B. It removes the accelerated-motion derivation and substantially revises low-pass energy analysis with finite-cutoff expressions and cube-versus-ball bounds in Appendix C.

C1.justification: V1 presents a two-component contribution combining motion losses with a learnable enhancement module. V2 instead centers its abstract, contributions, and conclusion on an architecture-independent spectral regularizer grounded in a unified SIM(2) framework. The claimed contribution changes substantially, while the general motion-quality objective remains.

C2.justification: V2 removes the claimed module/loss complementarity and adds explanations for separate spectral slices, including interference and conditioning problems with unified fitting. It interprets tilted-line scoring as rejecting non-rotational periodicity, discusses simple versus complex motion, and acknowledges failures even for simple SIM(2) prompts. The non-rigid-motion limitation remains.

D1.justification: Appendices A and D and Table 5 add spectral-grid sizes, Hann windowing, gating parameters, ridge and stability constants, loss weights, precision choices, and solver details. V2 also documents LoRA placement and reports 10–20% computational overhead. V1's prospective code-release statement disappears; neither PDF supplies an implementation link.

R1.justification: Most of the earlier literature survey is retained in compressed form. V2 adds supporting SIM(2), signal-processing, Hunyuan, and RAFT references, including Sharma and Duits and Reddy and Chatterji, while dropping Tian et al. It expands the positioning against flow, geometry, physics-rule, and test-time approaches without replacing the overall research context.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper, substantially rewrites the abstract and introduction, compresses related work, and reorganizes the method around the loss-only formulation. It also adds a reproducibility statement and structured appendices. The narrative revision extends well beyond inserting new experiments.

P2.justification: V2 switches from two-column to single-column layout, redraws the pipeline, removes the opening teaser, and replaces the canonical-motion illustrations. It merges the original backbone tables into Table 1, adds comparison and parameter tables, and relocates the unchanged user-study graphics into the appendix.

improvement.justification: V2 improves empirical assessment through the controlled Hunyuan/LoRA flow-loss comparison and makes implementation substantially more explicit. However, the added theoretical justification is internally inconsistent: Sections 3.5–3.6 say the surrogate losses upper-bound the unified residual, whereas Theorems B.5 and B.10 bound the losses by that residual. The concrete experimental and documentation gains support a limited overall improvement, rather than a substantial strengthening of the paper's theoretical reliability.
